metaDescription: Free online CSS formatter. Beautify minified CSS, including nested rules and @media blocks, with your choice of indent. Runs in your browser.
intro: Beautify CSS with one declaration per line and consistent indentation. At-rules such as @media and nested rules are indented, and strings and url() values are left alone.
why:
Minified stylesheets from a build, a plugin or a copied snippet are hard to read and impossible to review. Before you can find which rule sets a colour or why a media query misbehaves, you need the file laid out properly.

This formatter puts selectors on their own lines, writes one declaration per line, and indents the contents of @media, @supports and similar blocks, including nested rules. Strings, url() values such as data URIs, and comments are protected, so content like "a;b{" does not confuse it. It does not reorder properties or fix mistakes, so a missing semicolon stays missing. Formatting is done in your browser, and your stylesheet is not uploaded.
howTo: Paste your CSS into the input box.
Choose the indent: 2, 4 or 8 spaces, or a tab.
Read the formatted stylesheet in the output.

faq.a: No. It changes layout only: line breaks, indentation and spacing around punctuation. Selectors, properties and values are the same, and property order is not changed.

faq.q: Are data URIs and strings safe?
faq.a: Yes. Content inside quotes and url() is not touched, so base64 data URIs and strings with semicolons or braces are kept as they are.

faq.q: Does it support nested CSS and @media?
faq.a: Yes. @media and other at-rules are indented, and nested rules inside them or inside other rules get deeper indentation.
No. It does not validate. A missing semicolon or brace will still be missing in the output, though the layout may help you spot it.
